MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 28, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:06 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Scouts Ian Stanghelle, Hannah Corr, Jason Xue and Pacifica District Committee Chair
Tim Shank led the flag salute.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Administrative Analyst Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF
  FREE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – THIRD
  QUARTER 2020

Sharon Shapiro-Fox from Waste Management drew names for the 2nd and 3rd quarter
winners who will receive one free year of service:

  2nd QUARTER RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 2 Pinto Lane
  2nd QUARTER COMMERCIAL WINNER: Rolling Hills Investments

  3rd QUARTER RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 16 Pony Lane
  3rd QUARTER COMMERCIAL WINNER: Rolling Hills Montessori

5.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CAL WATER UPDATE ON PALOS VERDES PIPELINE PROJECT

Angie Gilbride from Cal Water provided an update on the Palos Verdes Pipeline Project,
reporting that all of the pipeline has been installed and tied into the Cal Water system.
The 30-day acceptance period will begin in early August, in which a stress-test is
performed, and by the end of August all of the paving will be completed. Cal Water is
planning a ribbon-cutting event in early September and hopes to have members of the
City Council in attendance.

Carmelo Sorce confirmed the paving on Montecillo Drive would be complete on Friday,
July 30, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN requested that the final project cost and apportionment
be shared with staff and Council. Angie Gilbride confirmed paving on Palos Verdes Drive
North will also be completed Friday, July 30 in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
ZERUNYAN.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 28, 2020
 Carmelo Sorce explained how and when the new pump house will work in combination
with the original pump station, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked the Cal Water team and City staff for the work done on this
2 ½ year project.

B.  PVPUSD UPDATE FROM SUPERINTENDENT DR. CHERNISS

Superintendent Alex Cherniss provided an update on the reopening of schools amidst the
latest Health Officer Orders. He reported that PVPUSD’s second Town Hall was held on
July 27 with over 2,000 viewers. School is still planned to begin August 26, but will begin
remotely. Parents can select a distance program for the year, or a hybrid model – half
time in school and half time at home. He summarized the recent efforts of the school
district, weekly meetings with Peninsula City Managers, and continued communication
with the community.

School Board Member Matthew Brach expressed his appreciation to Dr. Cherniss,
PVPUSD, and the all of the Peninsula cities’ staff.

Dr. Cherniss explained the K-6 school waiver allowed for by the Governor, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, and explained further that the school district is currently
waiting for the criteria required for the waiver in order to apply.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about what the School District is considering doing
for the children of families with working parents. Dr. Cherniss explained that the District
is reaching out to the local cities for locations with Wi-Fi to potentially hold programs for
those children.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked Dr. Cherniss and the School District, and
discussed the challenges in reopening that PVPUSD and higher education systems are
facing.

Dr. Cherniss stated that online curriculum was purchased by the District, which will drive
the education programs and will be the backbone for teachers to deliver the curriculum.
Teachers are being trained in online teaching, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
ZUCKERMAN. Dr. Cherniss explained that middle and high school students will still have
a six-period day with live online instruction, and elementary students will have three hour
blocks every day with live online instruction. A “boot camp” is being offered for free to any
student in the District, which will include two hours of math and two hours of English every
day leading up to the first day of school.

MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed her appreciation to District for being very inclusive and
thoughtful in its communications to parents and the community during this time. She
praised Dr. Cherniss and the School District staff for their work.

Dr. Cherniss stated he would like to come back quarterly to update the Council.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual

H.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JUNE 30, 2020

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the existing 286 units counting toward future
RHNA numbers. Community Development & Public Works Director David Wahba
explained that units already built or under construction are credited toward our existing
housing needs assessment, and confirmed the City cannot go back and lower the density.

Community Development & Public Works Director David Wahba confirmed the General

year, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Strawberry Lane Homeowners
  Association License Agreement for private security camera equipment located on

Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Attorney Davis explained that the risk and liability to the City is minimal, and that the

Administrative Analyst Slawson explained that the camera would be solar-powered, in

B.  AMENDMENT TO MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH PENINSULA
  CITIES AND PALOS VERDES PENINSULA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR
  COST SHARING TWO SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Amendment to the
  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified
  School District and the cities of Rancho Palos Verdes, Rolling Hills Estates, Palos
  Verdes Estates and Rolling Hills for cost sharing two school resource officers.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Manager Grammer explained that since the schools were closed in March, the cities
have not been charged for the school resource officers (SROs) who have been working
part-time. Once the schools reopen and there are students on campus, the cities will begin
to pay for the SROs’ services, either full-time or part-time depending on how the schools
reopen, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the outlined monthly activity report, wondering
when the report-out would occur. City Manager Grammer explained that the reporting has
been at the quarterly Regional Law Committee meetings.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the
live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media
platforms. No public testimony was received.
